api: rmsnorm_gated(x, weight, bias=None, z=None, eps=1e-5, group_size=None, norm_before_gate=True) -> Tensor; no aten registration
semantics: rms_norm_ref from mamba_ssm.ops.triton.layernorm_gated: gate applied before or after normalization, biased mean over group_size elements, float32 intermediates, result cast back to x.dtype

contract.x: (..., features), float32, float16 or bfloat16 on MPS for the Metal path
contract.weight: (features,), any float dtype; upcast to float32 for the kernel
contract.z: same shape and dtype as x, or None
contract.group_size: divides features; 16384 or less takes the register kernels, wider takes the streaming ones
contract.backward: analytic dx, dz, dw, db; weight gradient in weight.dtype

timings_method: each variant runs 3 to 20 calls per round with one torch.mps.synchronize at the end; the five variants of a shape -- fused forward, fused step, composed forward, composed step, and a same-shape copy_ floor -- are interleaved round by round inside one lease, so the machine load is common to all of them; median and min over 9 to 15 rounds are recorded, the ratios and before/after use min, the fused numbers include the python dispatch, and the composed numbers are the same arithmetic in torch ops on the same tensors
notes: one threadgroup per (row, group); the group's values stay in registers between the sum of squares and the write, so x, z and y cross the bus once each
a group wider than the register set streams: the same threadgroup walks it once for the mean square and once for the write, still one kernel

the wide backward is two kernels -- one threadgroup per row-group for c1, then one thread per feature column that walks its row block and writes a dw/db partial -- so a column is a register whatever the group width is
bfloat16 has no type in this MSL, so it is read as the top 16 bits of a float32 and written back rounded to nearest even, which matches torch's own cast bit for bit over 2^18 random values
the backward keeps dw and db in registers over a run of rows and reduces 256 partials in torch; measured cost over 192 to 1024 partials is flat within 5%, and 64 partials costs 70% on a 4096x768 step
float16 and bfloat16 accumulate in float32: squares, the mean and rstd never round to the narrow type, matching the reference's upcast
torch 2.14.1 silently returns zeros from mps.to('cpu', torch.float64) instead of raising, so the float64 reference converts in two steps
the gate order is the shader's enum: none=0, before normalization=1, after=2
limits: the streaming kernels re-read x and z for the write pass, so a group past the cutoff costs two reads of the input rather than one
the wide backward reads x, z and dy twice, once for c1 and once for the gradients

at the largest wide shapes the step is launch-bound, not bandwidth-bound: on 1024x65536 float32 the three kernels measure 2.2, 2.6 and 2.7 ms (366, 527 and 499 GB/s against a 421 GB/s copy_ floor) while the step takes 11.4 ms, so about a third of it is the per-launch cost this shared box charges; that cell is the one place where the fused step is 2.7x the composed chain rather than 4.2x or more, and a single-kernel wide backward -- one threadgroup per row-group walking the group in chunks of tgs*E, so dw/db stay in registers -- is how to remove it
the gate is silu only; a sigmoid or other gate would need another kernel
one threadgroup per row-group means a feature axis narrower than 32 leaves part of the first warp idle

16-bit lanes waste half of each memory transaction on this GPU: a bfloat16 copy measured 128 GB/s per element against 305 GB/s with two elements packed into one 32-bit access, and standalone forward kernels measured 1.36x (float32), 1.50x (float16) and 1.88x (bfloat16) for the paired form. Integrated into this kernel set the same templated accessor returned wrong values, which is why the shipped kernels still move one element per access; the paired path is the next thing to try, behind a correctness check at every depth and threadgroup width

the host is shared with other builds: absolute microseconds move by a factor of two between runs, so the interleaved speedup ratios are the stable part of these numbers and the min is the closer estimate of the kernel
a different machine, an M-series core count or a later torch will change the threadgroup heuristic, which was set from measurements of this one
